learning_objective: 🎯 Discover how specific diets are used as medicine to treat illnesses, speed up recovery, and the critical role dieticians play in hospitals!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is a specialized branch of nutrition focused on managing patients' nutritional needs in healthcare settings to treat, manage, or prevent diseases.

Diet therapy involves modifying normal diets to suit the needs of a sick person. This could mean changing the texture (liquid vs. solid) or altering specific nutrients (low salt for high blood pressure).
A normal diet can be changed into a Soft Diet (easy to chew/digest), Liquid Diet (clear or full liquid for post-surgery), or a nutrient-specific diet (like diabetic or low-sodium diets).
When patients cannot eat normally, they are fed via Enteral routes (using a tube directly into the stomach/intestines) or Parenteral routes (nutrients given directly into the veins through an IV).
Dieticians assess patient nutritional status, plan appropriate meals, counsel patients, and monitor their recovery in coordination with doctors.

fun_activity.title: 🥣 The Clear Liquid Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are a dietician for a patient recovering from digestive surgery. Write down a 1-day 'Clear Liquid Diet' menu. Remember, only things you can see through are allowed! (e.g., apple juice, clear broth, but NOT milk).

exam_tips: 📌 Always know the exact difference between Enteral feeding (using the GI tract via tube) and Parenteral feeding (intravenous/IV).
📌 Be able to give one example for why a 'Soft Diet' would be prescribed (e.g., dental issues or gastrointestinal problems).
📌 Remember that Clinical Nutrition focuses on 'disease management' while general nutrition focuses on 'health maintenance'.
quick_recap: ⭐ Diet therapy modifies normal food to meet specific medical needs.
⭐ Food consistency can be changed to clear fluid, full fluid, soft, or regular.
⭐ Clinical dieticians are essential members of the medical team, ensuring medications and nutrition work together.
